Set 1.text: A study finds that students who eat breakfast score higher in exams. The principal concludes that serving breakfast will raise the school's results. Which statement, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Some students dislike the food that would be served
Students who eat breakfast also tend to come from homes with settled routines and more study support
Breakfast improves concentration in the first hour of the day
Set 1.why: The conclusion assumes breakfast CAUSES the higher scores. A common third cause behind both is the classic confound and directly undermines causation. The others question scale or add supporting detail without touching the causal claim.

Set 1.text: 'The minister denied that the report had been suppressed.' Which of the following is NOT necessarily implied by this sentence?
options: Someone had suggested the report was suppressed
The minister spoke about the report
Set 1.why: A denial is a claim, not proof. Everything else follows from the sentence: the report exists, an accusation prompted the denial, and the minister spoke. Whether the suppression happened is exactly what is left open.

Set 1.text: Choose the pair whose relationship is most similar to CAUTIOUS : RECKLESS.
Set 1.why: Cautious and reckless are opposites along one dimension of behaviour. Diligent and careless are opposites in the same way. The other three pairs are near-synonyms.

Set 1.text: A shopkeeper marks a jacket 40% above cost, then gives a 25% discount on the marked price. What is the profit percentage?
Set 1.why: Cost 100, marked 140, sold at 140 x 0.75 = 105. Profit = 5 on 100 = 5%.

Set 1.text: A tank is filled by pipe A in 12 hours and by pipe B in 18 hours. Both are opened together, but pipe B is closed 3 hours before the tank is full. How many hours does filling take in total?
Set 1.why: Let total time be T. A runs T hours, B runs T-3. T/12 + (T-3)/18 = 1. Multiply by 36: 3T + 2(T-3) = 36, so 5T = 42 and T = 8.4 hours.

Set 1.text: The average age of 11 players is 28 years. When the coach's age is included, the average rises by 1 year. How old is the coach?
Set 1.why: Total of 11 players = 308. New average 29 over 12 people = 348. Coach = 348 - 308 = 40.

Set 1.text: All engineers in a firm can code. Some who can code are also designers. Which conclusion definitely follows?
options: Some people who can code are engineers
Set 1.why: 'All engineers can code' guarantees that engineers form part of the coding group, so some coders are engineers. The overlap between coders and designers need not include any engineer, so the first is not guaranteed.

Set 1.text: Five friends sit in a row of five seats. Ravi is in the middle seat. Sita is immediately to Ravi's right. Uma is immediately to Ravi's left. Tara is at the far left end. Where does Vik sit?
Set 1.why: Ravi is seat 3, so Uma is 2 and Sita is 4. Tara is seat 1. The only seat left for Vik is 5, the far right end.

Set 1.text: If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match was not cancelled. What follows?
options: The match was played in rain
Set 1.why: Denying the consequent of 'if P then Q' gives not-P. Since the match was not cancelled, it did not rain.

Each term is twice the previous plus a step that grows by 1: 3x2+1=7, 7x2+2=16, 16x2+3=35, 35x2+4=74, 74x2+5=153.

Set 1.text: A cube is painted red on all faces, then cut into 27 identical smaller cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
Set 1.why: In a 3x3x3 cube the edge positions (not corners) have exactly two painted faces. A cube has 12 edges with one such cube each, so 12.

Set 1.text: A square sheet is folded in half twice (left over right, then top over bottom), and a single hole is punched through all layers near the centre of the folded square. How many holes are there when it is unfolded?
Set 1.why: Two folds double the layers twice: 1 -> 2 -> 4 layers. One punch through 4 layers gives 4 holes.

Set 1.text: A school records subject enrolments: Physics 120, Chemistry 150, Biology 90, Maths 140. Students may take more than one subject and the school has 300 students. What percentage of total enrolments is Chemistry? (Round to the nearest whole number.)
Set 1.why: Total enrolments = 120 + 150 + 90 + 140 = 500. Chemistry share = 150/500 = 30%. The 300-student figure is a distractor - the question asks about enrolments, not students.

Set 1.text: A shop's sales were Rs 40,000 in April and Rs 50,000 in May; costs were Rs 30,000 and Rs 36,000. In which month was the profit MARGIN (profit as a percentage of sales) higher, and by how many percentage points?
Set 1.why: April margin = 10,000/40,000 = 25%. May margin = 14,000/50,000 = 28%. May is higher by 3 percentage points.

Set 2.text: A city introduced a congestion charge and traffic fell 18%. Officials credited the charge. Which finding would most strengthen their claim?
options: Traffic also fell 17% in a comparable city with no charge that year
Public transport use rose sharply in the same period
Traffic in comparable cities without the charge was unchanged that year
Set 2.why: A control group that did NOT change is what isolates the charge as the cause. Option 1 would weaken the claim; rising transport use is consistent with either explanation; revenue says nothing about traffic.

Set 2.text: Which word is closest in meaning to EPHEMERAL?
Set 2.why: Ephemeral specifically means lasting a very short time. Fragile and insubstantial concern strength or substance rather than duration.

Set 2.text: 'Few students passed the test' and 'A few students passed the test' differ because:
options: 'Few' emphasises how small the number is; 'a few' emphasises that there were some
'Few' is plural and 'a few' is singular
Set 2.why: 'Few' carries a negative emphasis (hardly any), while 'a few' carries a positive one (some). The distinction is emphasis, not count.

Set 2.text: A train travels 60 km at 30 km/h and the next 60 km at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
Set 2.why: Time = 60/30 + 60/60 = 2 + 1 = 3 hours for 120 km. Average = 120/3 = 40 km/h. The mean of the two speeds (45) is the trap.

Set 2.text: The price of a share falls 20% and then rises 20%. Compared with its original price, it is now:
Set 2.why: 100 -> 80 -> 96. That is 4% below the original, because the rise applies to the smaller base.

Set 2.text: A sum doubles in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become five times itself at the same rate?
Set 2.why: Doubling means interest equal to the principal in 8 years, so the rate is 12.5% per year. Five times means 4 x principal as interest, needing 4 x 8 = 32 years.

Set 2.text: Three boxes are labelled 'apples', 'oranges' and 'apples and oranges'. Every label is wrong. You may draw one fruit, without looking, from exactly one box. Which box should you draw from to work out all three contents?
Set 2.why: That box cannot be mixed, so it is purely one fruit and the single draw names it. Each other label then has only one wrong option left, which fixes the remaining two. Drawing from either other box leaves the mixed box ambiguous.

Set 2.text: Statement: 'Only members may enter the library.' Which of the following must be true?
options: Anyone who entered the library is a member
Set 2.why: 'Only members may enter' restricts entry to members - so anyone inside is a member. It does not oblige members to enter.

Set 2.text: In a certain code, MONDAY is written as NPOEBZ. How is FRIDAY written?
Set 2.why: Each letter shifts forward by one: F->G, R->S, I->J, D->E, A->B, Y->Z, giving GSJEBZ.
Each term is the previous doubled minus 1: 2x2-1=3, 3x2-1=5, 5x2-1=9, 9x2-1=17, 17x2-1=33, 33x2-1=65.

Set 2.text: A 4x4x4 cube is painted on all outer faces and cut into 64 unit cubes. How many unit cubes have NO face painted?
Set 2.why: The unpainted cubes form the inner 2x2x2 core: 8 cubes.

Set 2.text: A standard die has opposite faces summing to 7. If the top face shows 2 and the face towards you shows 3, what is on the bottom face?
Set 2.why: Opposite faces sum to 7, so the bottom is 7 - 2 = 5. The front face is irrelevant to the question.

Set 2.text: A company's revenue was Rs 200 cr in 2023 and Rs 250 cr in 2024. Its headcount went from 400 to 625. Revenue per employee has:
Set 2.why: 2023: 200/400 = Rs 0.50 cr per employee. 2024: 250/625 = Rs 0.40 cr. That is a fall of 0.10 on 0.50 = 20%.

Set 3.text: An advertisement claims: 'Nine out of ten dentists recommend this toothpaste.' Which question most usefully tests the claim?
options: How much does the toothpaste cost?
How were the dentists selected, and recommended over what alternative?
How many dentists are there in total?
Set 3.why: Sampling method and the comparison baseline are what determine whether the statistic means anything. Cost, total population and taste do not test the claim.

Set 3.text: Which sentence contains a logical, rather than grammatical, flaw?
options: Each of the students have submitted their work
Since every successful person reads books, reading books will make you successful
Running quickly, the bus was missed by him
Neither of the answers are correct
Set 3.why: The second reverses a conditional - a property of successful people is treated as a cause of success. The others are grammatical errors (agreement, dangling modifier, agreement).
A painter works ON canvas, the material worked upon. A sculptor works on marble. The chisel is the tool and the statue the finished product.

Set 3.text: Two friends invest Rs 30,000 and Rs 45,000 in a business. The first stays 12 months, the second 6 months. If the profit is Rs 35,000, what is the first friend's share?
Set 3.why: Capital-months: 30,000x12 = 360,000 and 45,000x6 = 270,000, a ratio of 4:3. The first friend takes 4/7 of 35,000 = Rs 20,000.

Set 3.text: A mixture of 60 litres has milk and water in the ratio 7:3. How much water must be added to make the ratio 7:5?
Set 3.why: Milk = 42, water = 18. For 7:5 with milk fixed at 42, water must be 30. So add 12 litres.

Set 3.text: The population of a town rises 10% in the first year and falls 10% in the second. If it is now 49,500, what was it originally?
Five books are stacked. Biology is at the top and English directly below it. Physics is above Chemistry, and Maths is below Chemistry. Which book is at the bottom?
Set 3.why: Biology is 1 and English 2. The remaining three must run Physics, Chemistry, Maths downward, so Maths is at the bottom.

Set 3.text: Three people make one true and one false statement each. A says: 'B lies. C tells the truth.' If exactly one of A's statements is true, which must be the case?
options: B tells the truth and C tells the truth
Either B lies and C lies, or B tells the truth and C tells the truth
B tells the truth and C lies
Set 3.why: Exactly one of A's two statements is true. If 'B lies' is the true one, then 'C tells the truth' is false, so C lies - giving B lies and C lies. If 'C tells the truth' is the true one, then 'B lies' is false, so B tells the truth - giving both truthful. Both scenarios satisfy the condition.

Set 3.text: Pointing at a photograph, a man says: 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is she related to him?
Set 3.why: The grandfather's only son is the man's father. The father's daughter is the man's sister.
Factorials: each term is multiplied by the next integer. 120 x 6 = 720.
8, 27, 64 and 125 are perfect cubes (2, 3, 4 and 5 cubed). 100 is a perfect square but not a cube.

Set 3.text: How many triangles are there in a triangle divided by joining the midpoints of its three sides?
Set 3.why: The four small triangles, plus the original large one, gives 5.

Set 3.text: A cube has faces numbered 1 to 6. Three views show: (1 top, 2 front, 3 right), (3 top, 1 front, 5 right), (5 top, 2 front, 4 right). Which number is opposite 2?
Set 3.why: Face 2 appears as front in views 1 and 3 alongside 1, 3, 5 and 4 - so 2 is adjacent to 1, 3, 4 and 5. The only remaining face is 6, so 6 is opposite 2.

Set 3.text: Marks in a class: 20 students averaged 60; another 30 students averaged 80. What is the combined average?
Set 3.why: Total = 20x60 + 30x80 = 1200 + 2400 = 3600 over 50 students = 72. The simple mean of 60 and 80 (70) is the trap.

Set 3.text: A budget allocates: Salaries 45%, Rent 15%, Marketing 20%, Other 20%. If Rent is Rs 3 lakh, what is the Marketing budget?
Set 3.why: Rent 15% = 3 lakh, so 1% = 0.2 lakh and the total is 20 lakh. Marketing 20% = 4 lakh.
